facts.statement: Gnathomortis is an extinct genus of marine lizards belonging to the mosasaur family.
facts.quote: Gnathomortis (meaning "jaws of death") is an extinct genus of marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.

facts.statement: Gnathomortis was a large mosasaur that measured 10.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a large mosasaur measuring 10.5 m long.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gnathomortis were recovered from the Early Campanian Mancos Shale in Colorado.
facts.quote: Fossils of Gnathomortis have been recovered from the Early Campanian Mancos Shale of Colorado.

facts.statement: The species was originally named Prognathodon stadtmani in 1999.
facts.quote: Gnathomortis was originally named as a species of Prognathodon in 1999.

facts.statement: Gnathomortis is classified in the class Sauropsida, order Squamata, superfamilia Mosasauroidea, and family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Sauropsida ordo: Squamata superfamilia: Mosasauroidea familia: Mosasauridae subfamilia: Mosasaurinae

facts.statement: The genus Gnathomortis was coined by Lively in 2020 for the species P. stadtmani.
facts.quote: Lively (2020) acuñó el nuevo género Gnathomortis para P. stadtmani.

facts.statement: Gnathomortis lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Gnathomortis es un género extinto de saurópsidos mosasáuridos que vivieron durante el Cretácico Superior, en lo que actualmente es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Gnathomortis lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2006 phylogenetic analysis suggested that Prognathodon stadtmani did not fit within the Prognathodon clade, leading to its reclassification.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis by Schulp et al. (2006) found that Prognathodon species coded in their analysis comprise one clade, but that "Prognathodon" stadtmani fell outside that clade, and as such did not fit in that genus.

rejected.statement: Lively moved the species to the new genus Gnathomortis in 2020 after further preparation revealed unique features of the quadrate and skull roof.
rejected.quote: further preparation of the specimen revealed unique features of the quadrate and skull roof, on the basis of which Lively moved it to the new genus Gnathomortis in 2020.
